00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — we wanted to understand your integration constraints (SDK, gateway, onramp), show how Redwood fits hosted/dedicated/private and then dig into observability and quotas.
00:18 Sofia Alvarez: Thanks Alex. We are evaluating options, we have a strict data residency requirement for EU but first we want to prototype in our dev region. Our main question is: do we route through our gateway or call Redwood SDK directly?
00:32 Alex Chen: Great. Can you describe your current flow? Marcus?
00:36 Marcus Lee: Sure, today our backend calls an internal proxy that does auth, rate-limits and routing to multiple LLM vendors. We want to add Redwood as a backend target, but keep the proxy in front - for auditing and A/B. We also evaluate embedding pipelines — LlamaIndex in some services.
00:58 Priya Kapoor: Just to clarify, are you planning to use Redwood Hosted API or a private deployment inside your VPC? That changes the recommended integration pattern.
01:08 Sofia Alvarez: Ideally hosted to start, but if we need strict egress controls we may want Dedicated or Private down the line. Security will decide.
01:18 Priyanka Singh: Correct — from security's perspective we need SSO (SAML), KMS integration for keys, audit logs with immutable retention, and the ability to keep PII out of long term logs. Do you have SOC2 and ISO stuff?
01:29 Alex Chen: Yes, we have SOC2 and a compliance pack — I'll share the summary after the call. We also support customer-managed keys in Private.
01:36 Jared Moss: For the SDK question — Redwood SDKs are small and idiomatic in node/python/go. If you're already doing proxy routing, calling Redwood from your proxy is a valid pattern; alternatively, you can use Lightweight sidecar or a gateway adapter. The tradeoff is where you enforce quotas and caching.
02:05 Marcus Lee: If we keep the proxy in front, we need consistent token accounting. Does Redwood expose token-level metadata in the response headers for observability?
02:15 Priya Kapoor: And do you surface per-request trace ids so we can join our traces in Datadog?

03:05 Alex Chen: Short answer — yes. Redwood returns per-request metadata: token counts, model id/version, latency buckets. We publish exporters and example integrations for Datadog, Prometheus, and Honeycomb. There is also a light-weight tracing header you can propagate — usually x-rwd-trace-id — to join logs.
03:30 Marcus Lee: Nice. And about quotas — can we enforce per-tenant limits from our proxy or do we use Redwood rate limits?
03:38 Priya Kapoor: We need to avoid double-enforcing in different layers.
03:41 Jared Moss: You can do both. Common pattern: enforce coarse quotas at your gateway, and use Redwood per-key rate limits to protect against spikes. Redwood supports token-based rate limits per API key and also per-model routing policies for burst capacity. There's an API to fetch current usage and quotas.

05:25 Alex Chen: (chuckles) batching is workload dependent. Redwood runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache reuse to reduce cost and improve throughput; but the SDK exposes sync and async helpers so you can opt out of batching for latency-sensitive calls. For LlamaIndex, we usually recommend keeping single-turn low-latency paths and enabling batch at the proxy for bulk generation jobs.

06:16 Marcus Lee: On private deployment — if we wanted to move to Private in our VPC, what parts of the control plane remain with Redwood? How does model updates work?
06:28 Jared Moss: Private keep control plane with Redwood for model catalog and billing, but compute can sit in your VPC or on-prem. We support signed manifests for model artifacts and version pinning. Rollouts can be canaryed by model version or by route. There are also options for offline onprem bundles if you need air-gap.
06:48 Priyanka Singh: KMS — can we bring our own key and have everything encrypted at rest with our key?
06:53 Jared Moss: Yes, BYOK supported in Private with integrations to AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM options. We'll document the flow.
06:59 Sofia Alvarez: One more: observability retention — our security wants 1 year of audit logs. Is that an add-on?
07:07 Alex Chen: Long-term audit retention is offered as an enterprise add-on. For Hosted we keep standard retention but can configure longer retention with an add-on. Dedicated and Private give you more control.
07:18 Marcus Lee: Latency SLAs — we care about 95th p95 under 300ms for short prompts. Can Redwood hit that from EU region?
07:28 Priya Kapoor: Also what's the tail latency behavior under burst?
07:32 Jared Moss: p95 depends on model size & sequence length. For small chat models and short prompt lengths, in a hosted EU region we regularly see p95 under 300ms for optimized endpoints; dedicated pools tighten that and private gives predictable hardware. We can run a perf probe against your traffic shape to validate.
07:52 Sofia Alvarez: That would be helpful. We'll share a sample of payloads.
07:56 Marcus Lee: Rate limiting detail — do you support token-based limits per API key, and separate quotas for embedding units?
08:05 Alex Chen: Yes. There's separate quota buckets and metering: generation tokens vs embedding units. You can set per-key limits and per-route overrides. There is also a quota API so your proxy can check allowance before forwarding.
08:21 Marcus Lee: Is there a webhook or push notification when quotas are hit, or do we poll?
08:25 Jared Moss: We have both: webhook alerts for critical quota thresholds and an audit API to poll usage. The webhook can be sent to your internal topic.
08:34 Priyanka Singh: About logs — we need to ensure PII is scrubbed. Can we configure automatic redaction?
08:41 Alex Chen: You can enable PII redaction rules at ingestion. For extra safety, Private gives you total control to avoid storing prompts at all.
08:52 Sofia Alvarez: Integration effort — overall how long to get an internal POC?
08:58 Alex Chen: Typical POC with SDK + proxy adapter and some observability onboarding is 2-4 weeks depending on availability. If you want Dedicated, procurement adds more time.
09:10 Marcus Lee: Ok. Let's talk technical specifics — auth. We use mutual TLS from our proxy to downstream services. Can Redwood support mTLS?
09:20 Jared Moss: For Private we support mTLS and IP allowlists. For Hosted we support standard TLS and JWT API keys; you can front the hosted API with your proxy and do mTLS on your proxy side, then proxied calls go out over TLS.
09:39 Marcus Lee: Are there any known incompatibilities with LlamaIndex? We saw some notes about kv cache semantics.
09:47 Priya Kapoor: I recall something about kv cache poisoning?
09:50 Jared Moss: The main caution is mixing batching and reuse of the KV cache. If you batch diverse contexts you can confuse cached state if the model has sessionful behavior. For RAG patterns with LlamaIndex, it's usually safe because you send a constructed context per request. We have a guide in the SDK docs about kv cache best practices (sometimes transcribed as KV cashe).
10:15 Sofia Alvarez: Great. Is there a recommended pattern for the proxy adapter? We use Envoy at the gateway.
10:23 Jared Moss: Many customers use an Envoy filter that annotates requests with tenant id, then forwards to Redwood. We have an open-source envoy adapter example. It handles token mapping, header propagation, and basic batching.
10:37 Marcus Lee: Could we get that example?
10:39 Jared Moss: Yes, I'll share the repo link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/envoy-adapter (note: example link).
10:48 Alex Chen: We'll also share a LangChain example repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/langchain-examples and a LlamaIndex snippet in the SDK docs.
10:55 Priya Kapoor: On quotas, if our proxy rejects locally to preserve budget, can Redwood be configured to return a specific error code so our proxy can map it?
11:03 Alex Chen: Redwood returns 429 with error details including quota bucket id and recommended retry-after. For embeddings we have a separate code path.
11:12 Marcus Lee: Regarding rollout, can we route a percentage of traffic to a new model via Redwood routing rules, not in our proxy?
11:19 Jared Moss: Yes, routing policies support weighted rollouts by model version and by region. You can control these from the console or via the API.
11:30 Sofia Alvarez: Any pitfalls to watch with cost/latency tradeoffs?
11:34 Alex Chen: Common pitfall: enabling aggressive batching to save cost but hurting latency for interactive flows. Also mixing quantized model variants across canaries can change output quality. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization levels by workload.
11:52 Priya Kapoor: Can you run a small pilot for us that demonstrates embeddings throughput and a retrieval flow with LlamaIndex?
11:58 Alex Chen: Yes. Suggested pilot: 1) send payloads and traffic shape, 2) Redwood runs perf probe and shares results, 3) we run a 2-week sandbox pilot with telemetry integration.

12:25 Alex Chen: Recap of what we'll share: compliance pack, envoy adapter repo, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, and a perf probe plan. Also sandbox access and step-by-step SDK quickstart.
